Niepolomice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Niepołomice, Poland

Not demolished. Jews probably settled in Niepołomice in the 18th century; by 1921, 484 (11.9%) were mostly killed in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the 19th century, held a WWI military section (War Cemetery No. 328) with Austro-Hungarian soldier Josef Austerweil among its burials; local Rabbi Josef Teitelbaum was interred there in 1936. Before 1939, the 30-acre grounds were enclosed by a stone wall with a funeral house at the entrance. Germans conducted executions here during WWII; by 1946, roughly half the tombstones were destroyed and the funeral house demolished, though the southern wall survived. As survivors emigrated, the Jewish community sought an agreement with city authorities over cemetery maintenance; eventually, at least half the plot was built over with single-family housing. Poland formally closed the cemetery on November 4, 1964. An ohel was built over Rabbi Teitelbaum's grave after 2014.
